{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-mi-s","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"0587293acbb0bc32fbbc209e7ed009e2b8568843b5d1726dd13f1716e0d7133d","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-mi-class-std:lineage:24","source_registry_sha256":"7af7437894a2c63b20529c8a1ed7c10696796036051dd6666178ab579008ca37","source_liveness_sha256":"e81e5179580dc89fb25fdf5194e9f75291db3aa019fc21ccfe32c38d1a9df42f"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Speed limits, work zones, emergency vehicles and school buses","heading":"C2 — Confusables and KG hints, speed limits, work zones, emergency vehicles and school buses","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Confusables and KG hints, speed limits, work zones, emergency vehicles and school buses

FACT_ID: sec06-R01 | anchor: A01
Cars may go up to 70 mph on a freeway, but school buses and trucks top out at 65 mph there, and at 55 mph on freeways posted below 70 mph. [A01]
Why it matters: group speed limits; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec06-F15, sec06-F16 [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-R02 | anchor: A01
The freeway minimum is 55 mph, the same number as the default limit on non-freeway highways, which is a maximum rather than a minimum. [A01]
Why it matters: group speed limits; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec06-F14, sec06-F15 [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-R03 | anchor: A01
Mobile home parks default to 15 mph, while platted subdivisions and condominium complexes default to 25 mph. [A01]
Why it matters: group speed limits; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec06-F11, sec06-F12 [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-R04 | anchor: A01
The posted limit is a ceiling, not a target: the Basic Speed Law can require driving slower when conditions demand it. [A01]
Why it matters: group speed limits; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec06-F10 [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-R05 | anchor: A02
Work zone speeding costs three points for 10 mph or less over, four for more than 10 up to 15 over, and five for more than 15 over, so even a small excess there costs three points. [A02]
Why it matters: group work zones; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec06-F23 [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec06-R06 | anchor: A02
A 45 mph work zone limit may apply only while workers are present; when they are gone, traffic may go back to the normal posted limit. [A02]
Why it matters: group work zones; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec06-F13, sec06-F21 [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec06-R07 | anchor: A02
Green flashing lights mark public road agency maintenance vehicles doing road work, while amber lights are the traditional maintenance color, and private contractors may not use green. [A02]
Why it matters: group work zones; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec06-F27, sec06-F28 [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec06-R08 | anchor: A03
For a stopped emergency vehicle you slow and move over, but for one approaching with lights and siren you pull to the edge and stop. [A03]
Why it matters: group emergency vehicles; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec06-F32, sec06-F35 [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-R09 | anchor: A03
Violating the move-over law near police, fire or ambulance vehicles is a civil infraction, but near utility or garbage trucks it is a misdemeanor. [A03]
Why it matters: group emergency vehicles; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec06-F33, sec06-F34 [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-R10 | anchor: A03
Follow a moving emergency vehicle no closer than 500 feet, yet stop at least 20 feet back from a school bus with flashing red lights. [A03]
Why it matters: group following distances; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec06-F37, sec06-F38 [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-R11 | anchor: A03
Oncoming traffic must stop for a school bus on an undivided road, but not when a barrier such as a median separates the lanes. [A03]
Why it matters: group school buses; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec06-F39 [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-R12 | anchor: A01
The unattended-child law covers children under 6, while back-seat seating is encouraged for all children 12 and younger. [A01]
Why it matters: group children; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec06-F02, sec06-F07 [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0040]
